chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: He (peace be upon him) is the first from whom I heard this word,

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الشَّرِيفُ: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī, the compiler of Nahj al-Balagha
key_terms.فَمَا عَدَا مِمَّا بَدَا: And what remained of what appeared (a specific phrase from the sermon)

ai.seo_question: Who was the first person from whom As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī heard the phrase 'Famā 'adā mimmā badā'?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi’s specific attribution of the phrase 'فَمَا عَدَا مِمَّا بَدَا' to Imam Ali underscores the precision of oral transmission (tawatur) in early Shia scholarship, validating the authenticity of Nahj al-Balagha’s sermons. This unique wording, delivered during the diplomatic mission to Zubayr before the Battle of the Camel, reflects the Imam’s rhetorical mastery in distinguishing between divine decree and human action, a key theological theme in Shia exegesis.
